title: Seven looks, one game
description: Original, classic filtering, warm lanterns and a moonlit night. Presets change presentation; the original game rules stay intact.

title: Light from the world
description: Recovered lantern surfaces emit warm light. The source, range and color come from scene assets and editable light rules.

title: Warmth from authored fires
description: The original fire and bonfire placements become real light sources. Compare their effect on nearby surfaces with fire lighting disabled and enabled.

title: Shape the pool of light
description: Light radius changes the area reached by an emitter. Ambient brightness controls how much baked light remains in shadow.

title: Choose the light and shadow budgets
description: Lamp and fire sources are discovered from the stage. More lights cover more of the scene; each shadowed point light requires six views.

title: Models cast real shadows
description: Scenery, characters and weapons occlude local lights. Compare unshadowed light, hard shadows and a softened edge.

title: Move a light around the player
description: A session-only light moves in world space. Watch the weapon and body shadows travel across the ground.

title: Shadow detail and softness
description: Shadow-map resolution controls detail; filtering softens the edge. The original ground-decal shadow remains a separate option.

title: Moonlight, from zero to full
description: A directional sky light adds cool outdoor illumination and model shadows. Local lantern light still fills the moon shadow.

title: Move the moon across the sky
description: Azimuth and elevation move the directional light and its shadows. Sky tint and light color shape the outdoor mood.

title: Choose a moon-shadow area
description: Directional-shadow coverage trades nearby detail for reach. Resolution is independent of coverage.

title: Four ways to sample a texture
description: Pixel, Smooth, Crisp and Cubic use the original artwork. Distance mipmaps and anisotropy remain a separate choice.

title: Keep distant textures stable
description: Nearest, bilinear, mipmaps and anisotropy trade shimmer for stable detail on surfaces viewed at an angle.

title: Reconstruct pixel contours
description: Compare original texels with Scale2x and Scale4x. Reconstruction can smooth pixel shapes; it cannot invent missing artwork.

title: Smooth silhouette edges
description: Cycle through MSAA levels supported by this GPU. Geometry edges become smoother without changing the source textures.

title: Separate artwork from shading
description: Texture and vertex-shading switches expose the original mesh and its baked illumination. Exposure lifts the resulting image.

title: Character contours and normals
description: Optional contour refinement and smooth model normals soften angular bodies. Animation, hitboxes and weapon behavior stay original.

title: 30 Hz logic, smoother motion
description: Compare original poses with visual interpolation. Intermediate rendered poses never enter collision, AI or game state.

title: Swap a body, keep the moves
description: Cycle compatible bodies discovered on the disc or in a model folder. The player keeps their animation, weapons and collision.

title: Contact shading
description: Screen-space occlusion adds depth where surfaces meet. Watch the ground, wall corners and nearby model contours.

title: Light spilling into the lens
description: HDR bloom spreads bright light into neighboring pixels. Its threshold and intensity are independent of the actual scene lighting.

title: Reveal the distance
description: Move the fog boundary and add colored haze. Free-camera views still use the same scene geometry and original collision map.

title: A different mood
description: Warm and cool grading, saturation and a restrained vignette change the final image. No replacement textures are required.

title: Tune the final image
description: Filmic mapping, contrast, gamma and sharpening refine the final image after lighting. Each control can be adjusted independently.

title: See what enemies see
description: Inspect actor labels, collision boxes, sight volumes and patrol paths directly inside the native runtime.

title: Change detection range
description: The sight multiplier changes enemy detection, not just the overlay. Standing and crouching bounds can also be inspected without changing AI.

title: Inspect the playable geometry
description: Collision surfaces, hazard colors and event regions reveal the structure under the artwork. These are the game’s own data.

title: Leave the gameplay camera
description: A free camera can orbit, inspect and frame a shot independently. F1 also offers bookmarks, actor focus and click-to-teleport.

title: Inspect, place and resume
description: Select an actor, inspect live state, then place the player on collision terrain. Teleports are explicit gameplay edits and end normal input recording.

title: Frame a clean photograph
description: Free camera, field of view, overhead framing and bookmarks help compose a shot. Photo mode hides the HUD and helpers; F9 saves a PNG.

title: Keep useful information close
description: The HUD, clear FPS display and compact F1 menu can be toggled independently. Menu/focus pause, audio, fullscreen and vsync remain host preferences.

title: Keep the whole stage awake
description: The optional activation override keeps distant guards updating. Gray labels indicate suspended actors; active patrols continue off camera.

title: Control simulation pacing
description: Slow motion and fast-forward execute the same ordered game ticks. F1 also offers single-step and unlimited simulation speed.

title: Inspect one game tick at a time
description: Pause and single-step advance the original 30 Hz state exactly once. Presentation and inspection remain responsive while gameplay is stopped.

title: Fast-forward a cinematic
description: Replay the same opening at 1x, 4x, then 16x. Every original script tick still runs; acceleration stops when the cinematic ends. Hold Backspace in normal play for maximum speed.

title: Measure a live frame
description: CPU history separates simulation, preparation, overlay and presentation. Supported GPUs also report asynchronous pass timings.

title: Your assets, live in the game
description: PNG/OBJ packs replace artwork with original assets as fallback. This compares the configured pack; without one, both views use disc art.

title: From sunrise to moonlight
description: A complete day in twenty seconds. Sun and moon shadows move across the original scenery; warm lamps remain visible after dark.

title: Rain on the rooftops
description: Rain hits roofs, runs down their slopes and drips over the eaves. Exposed surfaces gradually darken and reflect the sky; covered ground stays dry.

title: A fresh dusting of snow
description: Wind carries soft flakes through the scene. A thin coat gradually settles on exposed upward surfaces; walls and sheltered floors retain their artwork.

title: Ripples in the garden
description: The same pond alternates between original water and moving surface normals with sky reflections. The water remains in its original collision plane.

title: A softer waterfall
description: Curved render geometry rounds the waterfall lip while preserving its attachment edges. Fine mist follows the falling water; collision remains original.
